1	# Volta Studio — Strategic Design and Innovation Agency
     2	
     3	## Brand
     4	Volta Studio is a boutique strategic design and innovation agency creating Function + Feeling for industry-leading clients. Founded in Reykjavík, Iceland in 2014, Volta grew into a globally recognized studio before its founder joined a major tech company in 2021. In 2025, Volta reopened as a carefully curated agency working with a select number of enterprise clients.
     5	
     6	Brand colors: #000000 (primary black), #FFFFFF (white), #F5F5F5 (light gray)
     7	
     8	Tone: Minimal, editorial, warm. Copy is conversational and confident — first person, short sentences, no jargon.
     9	
    10	## Navigation
    11	- Volta. (logo/home)
    12	- Neweno
    13	- Services
    14	- Clients
    15	- Contact
    16	
    17	Mobile: Hamburger icon toggles full-screen overlay menu with all nav links.
    18	
    19	## Hero Content
    20	Title: "Hi. We're a strategic design and innovation studio."
    21	
    22	Below the headline, a media showcase section displays a triptych of editorial photography/video content spanning full width.
    23	
    24	## Client Marquee
    25	Three rows of client names scroll horizontally in a continuous marquee animation, each row moving in alternating directions.
    26	
    27	**Row 1:** Nexora ◦ Pinnacle ◦ Orbis ◦ Kinetic ◦ Lumina ◦ Helix ◦
    28	**Row 2:** Streamline ◦ Beacon ◦ Prism ◦ Zenith ◦ Forge ◦ Catalyst ◦
    29	**Row 3:** Vertex ◦ Horizon ◦ Atlas ◦ Meridian ◦ Crest ◦ Ember ◦
    30	
    31	## About Us
    32	ABOUT US
    33	
    34	We've worked with many of the most innovative companies in the world on large scale, strategic product and brand initiatives. We've built products used daily by hundreds of millions of people and created brands that changed industries.
    35	
    36	We've won multiple industry awards, including Webby Awards, Red Dot Design Awards, D&AD Pencils, Cannes Lions, FWA's, Awwwards, and many more. We've been named one of the Ad Age best places to work, and we landed on the Inc. 5000 with the fastest growing companies in the U.S. multiple times.
    37	
    38	In 2021 we joined a leading technology company to drive innovation. In 2025 we opened up again as a boutique agency working with a handful of carefully selected industry leading clients to create Function + Feeling.
    39	
    40	## Founder Letter
    41	Hi. My name is Erik. I'm the founder and CEO of Volta Studio. First of all, I want to say yes. Volta is back. I'm kind of surprised myself. I wasn't really planning on it. I started Volta in my apartment in Reykjavík, Iceland in 2014. And seven years later I sold it to a major tech company for a lot of money. But it wasn't the money. That's maybe hard to believe but that wasn't the reason. Business was great, I didn't need money. I needed a new challenge. Volta had grown over those seven years to multiple offices and over 100 people. We were working with the biggest brands in the world on some really exciting projects. But still, I felt like something was missing.
    42	
    43	I had been on the outside for a long time, working for companies to make something and then we'd hand it off to them to nurture and grow it. I wanted to be on the inside of a big company and see things through, to see them grow. I wanted a challenge and the biggest one I could find was leading innovation at a global platform. Things didn't turn out like I expected. But in hindsight that's not really what matters. We did some great work and I learned more than I could have imagined. About corporate ups and downs, and about my own ups and downs. I saw things you wouldn't believe. And then suddenly I was free and I went and made some other things. I built a lot of wheelchair ramps, I built a restaurant and movie theater, a bank, a recording studio, a community for creative people. I started a podcast, released a visual album, acted in some movies. I did everything I always wanted to do. And it was great. But after four years away from Volta it kept picking at me.
    44	
    45	This little itch. The feeling I get when someone comes with something that's just an idea and they want our help to see it become real. It feels like magic. Like alchemy. I missed that feeling. And so, yes, Volta is back. Blammo!
    46	
    47	## Philosophy
    48	**Function + Feeling**
    49	
    50	We believe things should work. That someone should make the effort to think it through, that the thing does the thing it's supposed to do, in the simplest way possible.
    51	
    52	But also, just as importantly, that it actually feels like people made it. That we feel the care that was put into making it, the connection from the creators to the person who interacts with the creation. So, on every project we start with two questions. What does it do? We call that Function. And, how does using it make people feel? We call that Feeling. And then we start creating.
    53	
    54	## Service Details
    55	**That's nice. But what do you actually do?**
    56	
    57	- **Branding.** All the elements about a company, product, experience — or to simplify it, brands — that make us feel something. Yes, it's a logo. And we've worked on a lot of those for some incredible clients. And yes it's colors. And typography. And how the brand talks (professionals call that voice and tone). And photos, videos, illustrations. How it moves, shakes and bakes. We do all that stuff.
    58	
    59	- **Products.** The ones we make are usually digital and they are usually pretty heavy on that function thing. It's an app, or a website, or a thingamajig, that does something. The button you push and a car shows up. Or the pizza. Whichever you prefer. But again it's also that feeling thing. Why do you keep coming back? Why don't you just use another app? Sure, maybe this app has better pizza, but maybe it's just more fun to use, maybe it makes you feel better but you can't explain why? Well, that's sort of what we do for some of the apps you probably use every day.
    60	
    61	- **Experiences.** The ones we make are again usually digital. Sometimes they are websites. Maybe it's a game where you drive a sleigh, or a website where you buy some perfume, or just a place you go to have some fun. Sometimes it's to sell something, usually there's a story to be told, usually there's a fair bit of branding involved. And you guessed it, we've done a lot of that for some of the biggest brands in the world.
    62	
    63	## Clients Grid
    64	**Clients** — Some of them.
    65	
    66	| Client | Description |
    67	|--------|-------------|
    68	| Nexora | Dozens of projects with teams across Maps, Cloud, Mobile, Mail, Drive, Play, Navigation, Video, Search, and more. |
    69	| Kinetic | We worked with Kinetic to re-brand the service as it expanded, leading to a new website and redesign of their core app. |
    70	| Pinnacle | We worked with the Pinnacle Maps team to build products to help businesses manage their services and find clients. |
    71	| Streamline | We've done multi-project engagements with the Streamline product, marketing and brand teams across multiple platforms. |
    72	| Orbis | Multi-year engagements with Messenger, Social, Video, VR, AI, and more, as well as a corporate re-brand. |
    73	| Lumina | We worked with the Lumina leadership team to create the biggest sports service in South America, across multiple platforms. |
    74	| Beacon | We've worked with Beacon to create partnerships with major partners and to develop new products. |
    75	| Prism | We worked with Store Lab, Prism's innovation unit, to create products like their innovative home delivery service. |
    76	| Zenith | We've worked with Zenith to develop their video service products as well as innovation for their physical shopping experiences. |
    77	| Forge | We worked with Forge to re-design their core apps on desktop and mobile and helped their sub-brand rebuild from the ground up. |
    78	| Catalyst | We worked closely with Catalyst to build their video product, launched across multiple platforms. |
    79	| Vertex | We initially worked with the brand and marketing team on a re-brand and a new website which led to product innovation. |
    80	| Horizon | We worked with the European convenience chain to create the fastest growing loyalty program in the local sector. |
    81	| Atlas | We worked with the brand and marketing team on a long term engagement across their main app and marketing channels. |
    82	| Meridian | We worked with Meridian from the early days of the service and onwards to design and develop products for their app and main website. |
    83	| Crest | We worked with Crest on a digital transformation project creating apps and services for their iconic venues. |
    84	| Ember | We worked closely with Ember leadership to design and build new products around safety, verification and faster checkout. |
    85	| Helix | We worked with Helix to create a comprehensive new product vision for the consumer and revenue side as well as a re-brand. |
    86	| Apex | Multi-year engagement, working with Apex on creating their innovative multi-platform streaming service and website. |
    87	| Stratos | Our first project with Stratos was to create their live news service, over the years this led to multiple engagements, including a full website redesign. |
    88	| Vantage | We worked with Vantage on their transformation from print first to digital first, designing a new website and app suite. |
    89	| Cirrus | Long term engagement including product design and development for Cirrus Banking, a pioneering new financial service. |
    90	| Mosaic | We worked with Mosaic on re-designing their sports platform from the ground up for web, TV's and new apps. |
    91	| Aether | We worked with Aether on their core platform experience and brand evolution across digital touchpoints. |
    92	| More | Other clients include Dropbox, ESPN, Nike, Samsung, Splunk, Allianz, Chubb, Spotify, Superhuman, Microsoft, Huawei, and so on. |

1 --- 2 name: ui-styling 3 description: Create beautiful, accessible user interfaces with shadcn/ui components (built on Radix UI + Tailwind), Tailwind CSS utility-first styling, and canvas-based visual designs. Use when building user interfaces, implementing design systems, creating responsive layouts, adding accessible components (dialogs, dropdowns, forms, tables), customizing themes and colors, implementing dark mode, generating visual designs and posters, or establishing consistent styling patterns across applications. 4 license: MIT 5 version: 1.0.0 6 --- 7 8 # UI Styling Skill 9 10 Comprehensive skill for creating beautiful, accessible user interfaces combining shadcn/ui components, Tailwind CSS utility styling, and canvas-based visual design systems. 11 12 ## Reference 13 14 - shadcn/ui: https://ui.shadcn.com/llms.txt 15 - Tailwind CSS: https://tailwindcss.com/docs 16 17 ## When to Use This Skill 18 19 Use when: 20 - Building UI with React-based frameworks (Next.js, Vite, Remix, Astro) 21 - Implementing accessible components (dialogs, forms, tables, navigation) 22 - Styling with utility-first CSS approach 23 - Creating responsive, mobile-first layouts 24 - Implementing dark mode and theme customization 25 - Building design systems with consistent tokens 26 - Generating visual designs, posters, or brand materials 27 - Rapid prototyping with immediate visual feedback 28 - Adding complex UI patterns (data tables, charts, command palettes) 29 30 ## Core Stack 31 32 ### Component Layer: shadcn/ui 33 - Pre-built accessible components via Radix UI primitives 34 - Copy-paste distribution model (components live in your codebase) 35 - TypeScript-first with full type safety 36 - Composable primitives for complex UIs 37 - CLI-based installation and management 38 39 ### Styling Layer: Tailwind CSS 40 - Utility-first CSS framework 41 - Build-time processing with zero runtime overhead 42 - Mobile-first responsive design 43 - Consistent design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) 44 - Automatic dead code elimination 45 46 ### Visual Design Layer: Canvas 47 - Museum-quality visual compositions 48 - Philosophy-driven design approach 49 - Sophisticated visual communication 50 - Minimal text, maximum visual impact 51 - Systematic patterns and refined aesthetics 52 53 ## Quick Start 54 55 ### Component + Styling Setup 56 57 **Install shadcn/ui with Tailwind:** 58 ```bash 59 npx shadcn@latest init 60 ``` 61 62 CLI prompts for framework, TypeScript, paths, and theme preferences. This configures both shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS. 63 64 **Add components:** 65 ```bash 66 npx shadcn@latest add button card dialog form 67 ``` 68 69 **Use components with utility styling:** 70 ```tsx 71 import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button" 72 import { Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardContent } from "@/components/ui/card" 73 74 export function Dashboard() { 75 return ( 76

Apply directive for component extraction 192 193 ## Visual Design System 194 195 **Canvas-based design philosophy, visual communication principles, and sophisticated compositions.** 196 197 See: `references/canvas-design-system.md` 198 199 Covers: 200 - Design philosophy approach 201 - Visual communication over text 202 - Systematic patterns and composition 203 - Color, form, and spatial design 204 - Minimal text integration 205 - Museum-quality execution 206 - Multi-page design systems 207 208 ## Utility Scripts 209 210 **Python automation for component installation and configuration generation.** 211 212 ### shadcn_add.py 213 Add shadcn/ui components with dependency handling: 214 ```bash 215 python scripts/shadcn_add.py button card dialog 216 ``` 217 218 ### tailwind_config_gen.py 219 Generate tailwind.config.js with custom theme: 220 ```bash 221 python scripts/tailwind_config_gen.py --colors brand:blue --fonts display:Inter 222 ``` 223 224 ## Best Practices 225 226 1. **Component Composition**: Build complex UIs from simple, composable primitives 227 2. **Utility-First Styling**: Use Tailwind classes directly; extract components only for true repetition 228 3. **Mobile-First Responsive**: Start with mobile styles, layer responsive variants 229 4. **Accessibility-First**: Leverage Radix UI primitives, add focus states, use semantic HTML 230 5. **Design Tokens**: Use consistent spacing scale, color palettes, typography system 231 6. **Dark Mode Consistency**: Apply dark variants to all themed elements 232 7. **Performance**: Leverage automatic CSS purging, avoid dynamic class names 233 8. **TypeScript**: Use full type safety for better DX 234 9. **Visual Hierarchy**: Let composition guide attention, use spacing and color intentionally 235 10. **Expert Craftsmanship**: Every detail matters - Hi. We're a strategic design and innovation studio.

About Us

We've worked with many of the most innovative companies in the world on large scale, strategic product and brand initiatives. We've built products used daily by hundreds of millions of people and created brands that changed industries.

We've won multiple industry awards, including Webby Awards, Red Dot Design Awards, D&AD Pencils, Cannes Lions, FWA's, Awwwards, and many more. We've been named one of the Ad Age best places to work, and we landed on the Inc. 5000 with the fastest growing companies in the U.S. multiple times.

In 2021 we joined a leading technology company to drive innovation. In 2025 we opened up again as a boutique agency working with a handful of carefully selected industry leading clients to create Function + Feeling.

© 2025 Volta Studio
Neweno Services Clients Contact

Volta.
Neweno Services Clients Contact
Volta. Neweno Services Clients Contact

Neweno

Hi. My name is Erik. I'm the founder and CEO of Volta Studio. First of all, I want to say yes. Volta is back. I'm kind of surprised myself. I wasn't really planning on it. I started Volta in my apartment in Reykjavík, Iceland in 2014. And seven years later I sold it to a major tech company for a lot of money. But it wasn't the money. That's maybe hard to believe but that wasn't the reason. Business was great, I didn't need money. I needed a new challenge. Volta had grown over those seven years to multiple offices and over 100 people. We were working with the biggest brands in the world on some really exciting projects. But still, I felt like something was missing.

I had been on the outside for a long time, working for companies to make something and then we'd hand it off to them to nurture and grow it. I wanted to be on the inside of a big company and see things through, to see them grow. I wanted a challenge and the biggest one I could find was leading innovation at a global platform. Things didn't turn out like I expected. But in hindsight that's not really what matters. We did some great work and I learned more than I could have imagined. About corporate ups and downs, and about my own ups and downs. I saw things you wouldn't believe. And then suddenly I was free and I went and made some other things. I built a lot of wheelchair ramps, I built a restaurant and movie theater, a bank, a recording studio, a community for creative people. I started a podcast, released a visual album, acted in some movies. I did everything I always wanted to do. And it was great. But after four years away from Volta it kept picking at me.

This little itch. The feeling I get when someone comes with something that's just an idea and they want our help to see it become real. It feels like magic. Like alchemy. I missed that feeling. And so, yes, Volta is back. Blammo!

— Erik

© 2025 Volta Studio
Neweno Services Clients Contact

Volta.

Volta. Neweno Services Clients Contact
Philosophy

Function + Feeling

We believe things should work. That someone should make the effort to think it through, that the thing does the thing it's supposed to do, in the simplest way possible.

But also, just as importantly, that it actually feels like people made it. That we feel the care that was put into making it, the connection from the creators to the person who interacts with the creation. So, on every project we start with two questions. What does it do? We call that Function. And, how does using it make people feel? We call that Feeling. And then we start creating.

That's nice. But what do you actually do?

Branding.

All the elements about a company, product, experience — or to simplify it, brands — that make us feel something. Yes, it's a logo. And we've worked on a lot of those for some incredible clients. And yes it's colors. And typography. And how the brand talks (professionals call that voice and tone). And photos, videos, illustrations. How it moves, shakes and bakes. We do all that stuff.

Products.

The ones we make are usually digital and they are usually pretty heavy on that function thing. It's an app, or a website, or a thingamajig, that does something. The button you push and a car shows up. Or the pizza. Whichever you prefer. But again it's also that feeling thing. Why do you keep coming back? Why don't you just use another app? Sure, maybe this app has better pizza, but maybe it's just more fun to use, maybe it makes you feel better but you can't explain why? Well, that's sort of what we do for some of the apps you probably use every day.

Experiences.

The ones we make are again usually digital. Sometimes they are websites. Maybe it's a game where you drive a sleigh, or a website where you buy some perfume, or just a place you go to have some fun. Sometimes it's to sell something, usually there's a story to be told, usually there's a fair bit of branding involved. And you guessed it, we've done a lot of that for some of the biggest brands in the world.

steps.message:
The Volta Studio corporate website is complete. Here's a summary of what was built:

### Output Files (`/app/output/`)
| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `index.html` | Homepage with hero headline, media triptych (terracotta/sage/sand blocks), 3-row client marquee, and about section |
| `neweno.html` | Founder letter — editorial long-form layout with drop cap, comfortable reading width, and personal signature |
| `services.html` | Philosophy ("Function + Feeling") + detailed service breakdowns (Branding, Products, Experiences) |
| `clients.html` | 25 client cards in a responsive 3-column grid with bold headings and descriptions |
| `contact.html` | Dramatic oversized "Contact" heading with Email, Instagram, and Twitter links |
| `styles.css` | Complete design system — warm cream palette, Playfair Display serif + Inter sans-serif, generous whitespace, responsive breakpoints |
| `main.js` | Mobile hamburger toggle with full-screen overlay, header scroll state, marquee content duplication for seamless loops |

### Key Design Decisions
- **Color palette:** Warm cream background (`#F5F2ED`), near-black text (`#1A1A1A`), terracotta/sage/sand accent blocks
- **Typography:** Playfair Display for editorial headlines, Inter for body text
- **Marquee:** CSS `@keyframes` with alternating directions (left/right/left), JS duplicates content for infinite seamless scrolling
- **Mobile nav:** Hamburger icon animates to X, full-screen overlay with staggered link fade-ins
- **Contact page:** `clamp(4rem, 15vw, 14rem)` heading that dominates the viewport
- **All pages** are fully self-contained HTML with relative paths — open directly in any browser with no build step
